A particular drug reduces symptoms of an illness for $75%$ of the patients in a trial. A new model of the drug is being tested, and the drug producer claims it is more effective than the previous model. Let $X$ be the number of patients in a random sample of $11$ that manifest a reduction of the symptoms after being treated with the new drug. Under the null hypothesis that the new model is as effective as the previous, what is the critical value of a one-tailed test at a significance level of $10%$?

*Hint: You may use the table below, representing the **probability mass function** of $X$ under the null hypothesis.*

| $x$ | $⋯$ | $6$ | $7$ | $8$ | $9$ | $10$ | $11$ |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| $P(X = x)$ | $⋯$ | $0.0803$ | $0.1721$ | $0.2581$ | $0.2581$ | $0.1549$ | $0.0422$ |

> A scientific calculator is required to answer this question.

The average number of monthly traffic incidents on a particular road is $2$. Some citizens think that removing a nearby semaphore will increase the number of incidents.
Let $X$ represent the number of incidents on that road during a one-month period after removing the semaphore. Under the null hypothesis that the number of incidents is the same as before, what is the critical value of a one-tailed test at a significance level of $10%$?

*Hint: You may use the table below, representing the **cumulative distribution function** of $X$ under the null hypothesis.*

| $x$ | $⋯$ | $2$ | $3$ | $4$ | $5$ | $6$ | $⋯$ |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| $P(X \le x)$ | $⋯$ | $0.6767$ | $0.8571$ | $0.9473$ | $0.9834$ | $0.9955$ | $⋯$ |

> A scientific calculator is required to answer this question.
